name: Every top-up run leaves an append-only record of what it attempted
notes: UPDATED goal-desk-iter-23 by browser-qa-agent: the previous version of this script asserted the honest-empty 'No top-up runs recorded yet.' text at step 2. That text is no longer true against the ambient apps/backend/.data/ store -- a real top-up run (id topup-2026-07-29-5de907c83fc4, state done, 404/404 pairs attempted, 0 reused / 390 fetched / 14 failed) landed on the ambient store between iter-11 and iter-23, exactly the honest environmental drift the original script's own notes predicted ('If a future operator-run top-up ever lands a real record on the ambient store, this step will fail for an honest environmental reason ... rather than a product regression -- update the expected text'). Re-verified live in goal-desk-iter-23: /desk's Top-up Runs section and LATEST RUN detail render this real record correctly (table row, state/attempted-of-total stats, per-outcome counts, and all 14 failed pairs' verbatim detail legible) -- confirmed via DOM text extraction AND a real screenshot (reports/qa/goal-desk-iter-23-evidence/UT-J-09-topup-runs.png + crops). This is a stale-golden repair, not a regression fix.

This replay script is DELIBERATELY READ-ONLY (goto only, no click) so it never mutates whichever backend/.data store is live at replay time -- J-09 ships no new interactive control (OUT OF SCOPE: 'no new button or control ships this iteration'), and the one pre-existing control that could produce a NEW recorded run (the J-02 'Top-up' button) triggers a real ~100-symbol walk against the vendor adapter, which this era's own NOTES/anti-goals reserve for an explicit, separately-reported operator act -- never an automated regression lane (the iter-4/iter-5 write-triggering-golden lesson).

Step 2's expected text '404 of 404 pairs attempted' is the CURRENT ambient store's real latest-run stat line (GET /research/desk/topup/runs's own payload rendered verbatim), not decorative chrome. Like J-08's dated history rows, this value is itself environment-dependent -- if a further real top-up run is ever recorded on the ambient store, this step will again need updating to that run's own stats (an honest environmental change, not a regression), the same class of environment-dependency the previous version of this note documented for the empty state.

Step 3 is a post-match liveness check (this era's iter-4/iter-5 lesson): a further /desk navigation AFTER the key text match, proving the page is still alive and rendering correctly, not merely that the match happened a moment before a crash.
